rows.subtype: Living for the moment with costs [Actor]
rows.description: A young adult quits a job in anger, spends the month's money in a week or ends a relationship in a flash. Excitement or upset drives the decision; building a delay habit and support saves regret.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: anger, excitement, regret

rows.description: A partner or family member sees repeated sudden choices that affect shared money or plans and feels anxious. Calm agreements about big decisions, without contempt, help; persistent trouble deserves professional guidance.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: contempt, anxiety, calm

rows.description: A child cries when a treat is delayed and asks are we there yet repeatedly. Patience grows with age and with adults who make waiting concrete through timers, songs and small games.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A child begins to save pocket money for a toy or wait a turn without complaint. Realises that waiting can bring more, and enjoys the pride of having managed it.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager wants instant results in fitness, skills or friendships and gives up when improvement is slow. Seeing progress in small steps and comparing to their own earlier self builds patience.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 23–26

rows.description: A wise adult stays calm with a slow learner, a long process or a difficult relative, knowing pushing rarely speeds growth. Patience is not passivity; it is choosing pace with purpose.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17

rows.subtype: Big feelings in a small body [Actor]
rows.description: A toddler screams with joy or falls to the floor in rage over small things and cannot yet calm alone. Intensity is a temperament, and calm adult presence is the way children learn to settle.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: joy, anger, calm

rows.description: A child loves fiercely, gets crushed by teasing and has long, loud upsets. Naming feelings and teaching ways to cool down turn intensity into passion rather than trouble.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A teenager feels intense crushes, rage at unfairness and deep sadness, sometimes within one day. Hormones and a developing brain amplify emotion; it is often normal but needs steady adults.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 18–22

rows.description: A parent or sibling faces slammed doors and dramatic outbursts and feels walked on. Staying calm, holding limits on behaviour and talking after feelings settle keeps connection.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 18–22
